3.text: 1. INCANTATIONS FOR TAMING WILD REINDEER-BUCKS WHO HAVE JOINED

5.text: (a) It is a wonder, it is a wonder. I tugged at your heart’s life

6.text: (tetkeˊyuñ),¹ together with the aorta. I drew it out of your anus, and appro-

7.text: priated it to myself. (The person practising the incantation picks up from

8.text: the footprint of the animal two splinters or blades of grass, and puts them

9.text: into his left mitten. On coming home, these must be wrapped in a piece of

10.text: leather, and suspended in the inner room, over the lamp.) It is a wonder,

11.text: it is a wonder. I drew out your psalterium, I took it out of your anus and

12.text: put it over your nose, like a bag. It is a wonder, it is a wonder. I make

13.text: you into a tame doe. How is it? Go and look for a husband among the

14.text: people of the Morning-Dawn! It is a wonder, it is a wonder. You have

15.text: brought the son of the heaven’s crack. It is a wonder, it is a wonder.

16.text: You have brought the son of the Morning-Dawn’s top.² It is a wonder, it

17.text: is a wonder. You have brought the son of the “separate clouds.” It is a

18.text: wonder, it is a wonder. I have put you on a broad rock. It is a wonder,

19.text: it is a wonder. I have put you on a large rock. It is a wonder, it is a

20.text: wonder. I have put you in a large ravine. It is a wonder, it is a wonder.

21.text: With the stones falling down from both sides, I made your eyes unseeing.

22.text: It is a wonder, it is a wonder. With the stones falling down from both

23.text: sides, I made your ears unhearing. How is it? I fastened stones to the

24.text: points of your hair. How is it? O Zenith! give me your striking-stone.

25.text: (The person practising the incantation appears as if about to take something

26.text: with his left hand.) I will put it on this one’s crown, among the antlers.

27.text: How is it? I have put you on a large lake. It is a wonder, it is a wonder.

28.text: I put you with unseeing eyes on a glacier which is splitting with great noise.

29.text: How is it? O Zenith! give me your forked wood; I will put it on this one’s

30.text: neck. It is to be trampled upon by the herd from both sides.

31.text: I ask an incantation from the World (Ñaˊrg̣ɪnên). I beg from the Front

32.text: Head (the star Arcturus)³ the right-side reindeer of his team and that most

33.text: thoroughly broken reindeer that leads the train of his sledges. I tie the aorta

34.text: of the wild reindeer-buck to these two. From the top of the Zenith I haul

35.text: down the heart’s life (tetkeˊyuñ), and with this I strike you on the head.

36.text: After that I cry out, “Ka, ka, ka!” but he cannot fly, being tied up. The

37.text: Pebbly River (the Milky Way) I make for my road. I call the East and the

38.text: West Wind to bring me smoke from every camp around. Then I build a

39.text: big fire before the entrance of my tent, and I say, “You are my chief guest!

40.text: Come in! Let us feast at my house; let us eat. What is the best? You
